transition_judgments.evidence: Projection and two-dimensional inverse become three-dimensional row equations, reciprocal dot pairing and plane spacing. Fresh reads02.04,03.04,04.04 show actual explanation, arithmetic and answered diagnostics; the pre-L05 fraction repair gate closes pacing risk.

Node/sheet and half-open ownership definitions feed explicit digit and finite-list operations.06.04 explains representatives versus equality;07.04 proves its E hypotheses on pairs and retains a counterexample, so abstract vocabulary does not hide prerequisite theory.

Ratio normalization precedes carried integer/residual records and dimensionless logs.09.04 derives both recurrence routes and parity inversion;10.04 derives and inverts J with fixed-angle and scalar-scope restrictions.

Small incidence ranks and tree/chord coordinates support later matrix reading.12.03 derives eigenvalues by component equations and zero/nonzero cases;13.03 constructs transfers, roots and drawings before Cartan names. Dimension recurrences retain carrier labels.

Finite operations prepare complex group actions;14.05 starts with a mod6 toy before exact source kernel.15 subset census precedes16.02 signed contraction and dual covariance. Capstones assess these operations, not an unintroduced group-classification proof.

Adjoints, ordered actions and retained states carry into shifts, phases and projectors.18.02 explicitly contrasts square/rectangular/infinite domains;19 capstone retains all factors, tau and sectors;20.07 derives scalar elimination and handles singular branches before synthesis.

Rank and coordinates support the explicit decoder and character map;21.03 derives its six equations and actual four-character inverse.22.04 supplies its own finite geometric-sum/tail and matrix-norm proof. Neither transition presumes a general spectral or functional-analysis theorem.

History/domain discipline is retained when reading M19 extensions.23.04 proves finite graph counts and labels cohomology/exceptional source cards as premises and missing constructions; its assessment asks calculations or precise missing-input specifications.

24.04 explains the limited derivative rules used by prescribed trajectories.25.05 then handles finite event interpolation, continuity, contact, jump and gap explicitly; general moving-ruler differentiation remains outside required computation.

Frames, signed projection and passage phase feed harmonics.26.05 derives the four-count inverse and parity nullspace;26.06 preserves interval signs and transfer ambiguity;26.07 retains all14 signed source rows and provenance gaps.

Typed velocities and ruler rates feed a distinct phase form, not a replacement Gram metric.27.05 proves the finite lower bound over declared paths;27.06 audits actual missing source-certificate fields without claiming a toy replay closes them.

Synthetic laboratory rehearsal combines keys, event supports and inverses.28.04 distinguishes centered reflection from periodic half-turn, teaches both decompositions and DFT inverse, and retains odd components missed by an even comparator.

Angular conventions and Gram geometry support separately typed galaxy maps.Prior full independent29 review covers all8 lessons; current hash is pinned. Unit-sphere length is not nm/Mpc calibration; phase offsets are not centers; half-open owner is not nearest center under a skew metric.

All30 nodes lie in the final prerequisite closure.30.01 explicitly restores18 core modules, six premises and supplied states while retaining M19 separately.30.08 teaches the small decoder and six factors before the capstone; proposed ruler/transfer, calibration gap and every outcome branch are explicit.
